quotes.text: In the Appropriations Committee, we have certainly not agreed with the down funding on machine learning an AI, so we have tried to fund government in those areas. Not just in the military, but in applications across the spectrum. We’ve got to keep a coordinated focus in AI.

AI is changing our world and the pace of change is accelerating. It is all of exciting, uncertain and concerning, and many constituents asked me for more information on AI and how it may affect us. In response, I hosted a live webinar last Friday, June 7th, with special guest Austin Bonner of the White House’s Office of Science and Technology Policy who is at the center of our national and international discussion of AI.

Artificial intelligence: what is it; how will it affect us; what are our policy choices to maximize its opportunities and minimize its risks? By constituent request, I’m discussing all of this in a live webinar on Friday, June 7 starting at 9 AM Hawaiʻi Time… (1/3) https://t.co/32jvHamgYH

Really impressed by the great beginning sixth grade students and their teachers at first-year Kūlia Academy Public Charter School, located at St. John the Baptist Church in Kalihi, “the first school in the U.S. to offer a comprehensive seven-year artificial intelligence/data science education program”. Watching the next gen hi-tech leaders in the making.
We do not want a patchwork of inconsistent laws and regulations across the country, where there’s perhaps too much regulation in some places or too little regulation in some places,

Political candidates should have to disclose if their campaign ads have AI-generated content. I joined my colleague Rep. Joe Morelle (NY), senior Dem on our House Administration Committee, in sponsoring legislation to “provide further transparency for the use of content that is substantially generated by artificial intelligence in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image, audio, or video footage in the advertisements.” More: https://t.co/9WqDVA5D4h

I happen to spend most of my time in Congress in national defense, and artificial intelligence is critical to national defense. And our adversaries are definitely pursuing artificial intelligence. And that's going to shape national defense.

But where there are identifiable gaps that raise serious harms, Congress should determine whether legislation that's appropriately tailored is necessary and we should work hard to implement it. I don't think we should begin from either extreme, you know, that the government should regulate every single thing or that Congress should simply ignore legitimate risks.
